documents.title: Standards and Recommendations for the Use of Generative AI in Teaching and Learning at Northeastern
documents.summary: July 2025 provost standards for teaching with generative AI. Instructors set the rule for their courses and must communicate it in the syllabus, assignments and class; the document supplies sample syllabus statements and assignment labels, recommends disclosure, process-focused assessment and discourages AI detectors, and requires AI Review Committee approval for some instructor uses.
documents.stance_why: The document says "The university supports faculty autonomy in determining appropriate AI use in their courses" and "It is up to each faculty member to determine the appropriate use of AI". It offers sample statements (encouraged, sometimes allowed, not permitted) and four assignment labels, so it sets no stance itself and delegates.

documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy
documents.summary: The university academic integrity policy defines cheating, fabrication, plagiarism and related violations and the reporting, sanction and appeal process. AI appears once, as an unauthorized aid in the definition of cheating.
documents.stance_why: Cheating includes "Unauthorized use of aids such as ... artificial intelligence, chatbots"; AI is banned unless the instructor authorizes it, which is restrict. The policy says nothing more on AI.

notes: Coder B. Only the four included documents were coded; neu-catlr-2023 was screened out. The AI Policy page (neu-ai-policy) is a stub; the full Policy on the Use of AI Systems was not in the collected text. Integrity-policy units on sanctions, appeals and reporting are generic to all violations and were coded because AI use is classed there as cheating. Unit stance for sample labels is that of the label itself.
